title: Case 1: Citizenship at Commencement (Domicile, Birth & Residence) (Article 5 • Writ Petition)
factualMatrix: Before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32), an aggrieved petitioner challenged an impugned executive notification and enforcement order issued by the Union Ministry / Central Authority under Article 5 (Citizenship at Commencement (Domicile, Birth & Residence)) of Part II (Citizenship). Relying on the core guarantee that Conferred citizenship on 26 January 1950 upon every person having domicile in the territory of India who fulfilled one of three conditions: born in India, either parent born in India, or ordinarily resident in India for at least five years preceding... and citing State of UP v. Rehmatullah (1971), the petitioner sought judicial invalidation for violating constitutional limits and procedural fairness.

modelAnswer:
1. MAINTAINABILITY: The Writ Petition before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32) is maintainable as it raises a direct constitutional question under Article 5 (Part II).

2. SUBSTANTIVE ANALYSIS (Article 5): Conferred citizenship on 26 January 1950 upon every person having domicile in the territory of India who fulfilled one of three conditions: born in India, either parent born in India, or ordinarily resident in India for at least five years preceding... Applying the governing principle—'Single Citizenship: India maintains a unitary citizenship model with no dual state citizenship.'—the impugned executive notification and enforcement order by the Union Ministry / Central Authority must strictly satisfy constitutional bounds.
